result.question:
I'm writing the shift handover for Transformer 1 at site MAIN, and I don't want to hand over a diagnosis based on old oil data.

First, tell me when the newest oil sample was taken and how old it is in days. Give me the full data span and the number of samples.

Then give me two findings from the latest complete sample:
- A dissolved gas fault classification from hydrogen, methane, ethane, ethylene and acetylene.
- A health index and condition category, using those five gases plus co, co2, oxygen, nitrogen, dbds, interfacial_v and dielectric_rigidity.

Next, list every open and pending-approval work order on Transformer 1 with its number, description, priority and scheduled date.

Decide as follows:
- If the newest sample is more than 30 days old, treat both findings as not current. Label them 'stale' in the handover.
- In that case, if no open work order already covers oil sampling, create one. Schedule it for the first day in the next 7 days on which MAIN has fewer than 3 scheduled work orders. Make it priority 2 if the health index is fair or worse or the class is D1, D2 or T3, and priority 3 otherwise.
- If the sample is 30 days old or less, don't create anything. Just summarize the findings.

Finish with a short handover note of no more than five lines.

If the health index can't be computed because an input is missing, name the missing input. Base the priority on the gas classification alone, and don't estimate the missing value.
result.answer:
The newest oil sample for Transformer 1 is about 986 days old, so both findings below are stale. Work order 1000052 already covers oil sampling, so I did not create a new one.

**1. Oil data freshness**
- **Newest sample:** 2024-01-19 00:00 UTC, which is about 985.9 days before now (2026-09-30).
- **Data span:** 2024-01-15 to 2024-01-19, with one sample per day.
- **Number of samples:** 5.
- The newest sample is complete: all 30 fields have values. `water_content` reads 0, which is unusual.

**2. Findings from the 2024-01-19 sample (both stale)**
- **Gas fault classification: T2, a thermal fault between 300 and 700 °C. I worked this out by hand because the gas analysis tool failed twice ("LLM unavailable").**
  - Gas levels: H₂ 2850, CH₄ 7400, C₂H₆ 5470, C₂H₄ 16650 and C₂H₂ 7 ppm.
  - Ratios: C₂H₂/C₂H₄ = 0.0004, CH₄/H₂ = 2.60 and C₂H₄/C₂H₆ = 3.04.
  - Under the IEC 60599 ratio rules, that pattern is T2. It would only be T3 if C₂H₄/C₂H₆ were above 4.
- **Health index: 72.4, condition "Good".** No input was missing. The model also needed `power_factor` (1) and `water_content` (0), and both came from the same sample.
  - This score doesn't fit the very high gas levels. The total combustible gas is about 32,400 ppm, which is Condition 4, the worst level under IEEE C57.104.

**3. Open and pending-approval work orders on Transformer 1**

| WO | Status | Description | Priority | Scheduled date |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1000053 | WAPPR (pending approval) | Outage + inspection Transformer 1, 2024-01-20..21 (C57.104 Cond 4) | 1 | None set (proposed window in the text is 2024-01-20..21) |
| 1000052 | APPR (open) | Confirmatory DGA oil sample - Transformer 1 (worst-case TDCG forecast IEEE C57.104 Condition 4) | 1 | None set |
| 1000051 | APPR (open) | OLTC inspection - Transformer 1 on-load tap changer (suspected contact wear/coking) | 1 | None set (target start in the text is 2024-01-19) |

**4. Decision**
The sample is more than 30 days old, so both findings are labelled stale. WO 1000052 is already an open oil-sampling order, so I created nothing. Had one been needed, it would have been priority 3: the health index is Good and T2 is not one of the priority-2 classes (D1, D2 or T3).

**Handover note**
1. Transformer 1 at MAIN: the newest oil sample is from 2024-01-19 (about 986 days old). The data span is 2024-01-15 to 2024-01-19, with 5 samples.
2. Stale findings: gas classification T2 (thermal, 300–700 °C; worked out by hand because the tool was down) and health index 72.4 "Good".
3. Gas levels were at Condition 4 (worst) when last sampled. Treat the unit as unconfirmed until a fresh sample comes back.
4. Open work: 1000052 (oil sample, approved, priority 1), 1000051 (tap changer inspection, approved, priority 1) and 1000053 (outage, waiting for approval, priority 1). None has a scheduled date.
5. Action: schedule and carry out oil sample WO 1000052 first. No new work order was raised because 1000052 already covers it.
